nodes.summary: Let $X$ be an irreducible scheme over a scheme $S$. The birational automorphisms of $X$ over $S$ form the subgroup of the group of birational self-maps of $X$ consisting of those birational maps whose forward rational map $X \dashrightarrow X$ is compatible with the structure maps to $S$.
nodes.title: Birational automorphisms over a base

nodes.summary: Let $X$ and $Y$ be irreducible schemes. A birational map from $X$ to $Y$ consists of dominant rational maps $f \colon X \dashrightarrow Y$ and $g \colon Y \dashrightarrow X$ that are mutually inverse: $g \circ f$ is the identity rational map of $X$ and $f \circ g$ is the identity rational map of $Y$.
nodes.title: Birational map

nodes.summary: For a field $k$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the Cremona group $\mathrm{Cr}_n(k)$ is the group of birational automorphisms of affine $n$-space $\mathbb{A}^n_k$ over $\operatorname{Spec} k$.
nodes.title: Cremona group

nodes.summary: For a field $k$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$, this is the proposition that the Cremona group $\mathrm{Cr}_n(k)$ is generated, as a group, by its pseudo-regularizable elements.
nodes.title: Cremona group generated by pseudo-regularizable elements

nodes.summary: Let $X$ and $Y$ be irreducible schemes over a scheme $S$. A birational map from $X$ to $Y$ is over $S$ when its forward rational map $X \dashrightarrow Y$ is compatible with the structure maps to $S$.
nodes.title: Birational maps over a base

nodes.summary: Let $X$ and $Y$ be schemes. A partial isomorphism from $X$ to $Y$, that is, an isomorphism $U \cong V$ between dense open subschemes $U \subseteq X$ and $V \subseteq Y$, is a pseudo-isomorphism if it is an isomorphism in codimension one: every point of $X$ outside $U$ and every point of $Y$ outside $V$ has coheight at least $2$ in the specialization order of points.
nodes.title: Pseudo-isomorphism

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a variety over a field $k$. A birational automorphism $\varphi$ of $X$ is pseudo-regularizable if there exist a variety $X'$ over $k$, a birational map $\alpha \colon X \dashrightarrow X'$ over $k$, and a partial isomorphism $\gamma$ from $X'$ to itself over $k$ that is a pseudo-isomorphism (an isomorphism in codimension one), such that $\varphi = \alpha^{-1} \circ \gamma \circ \alpha$, where $\gamma$ is…
nodes.title: Pseudo-regularizable birational automorphism

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a variety over a field $k$ and let $\varphi$ be a birational automorphism of $X$. A pseudo-regularization of $\varphi$ consists of a variety $X'$ over $k$, a birational map $\alpha \colon X \dashrightarrow X'$ over $k$, and a partial isomorphism $\gamma$ from $X'$ to itself over $k$ that is a pseudo-isomorphism, such that $\varphi = \alpha^{-1} \circ \gamma \circ \alpha$, where $\gamma$ is viewed as a…
nodes.title: Pseudo-regularization of a birational automorphism

nodes.summary: For an irreducible scheme $X$, the identity birational map of $X$ has the identity rational map of $X$ as both its forward and its inverse map.
nodes.title: Identity birational map

nodes.summary: Let $X$ and $Y$ be irreducible schemes. The inverse of a birational map from $X$ to $Y$ is the birational map from $Y$ to $X$ whose forward map is the inverse rational map of the original and whose inverse map is its forward rational map.
nodes.title: Inverse birational map

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a number field. The Cremona group $\mathrm{Cr}_3(k)$, the group of birational automorphisms of affine $3$-space over $k$, is not generated by its pseudo-regularizable elements.
nodes.title: $\mathrm{Cr}_3$ of a number field is not generated by pseudo-regularizable elements

nodes.summary: $\mathrm{Cr}_3$ of a function field over a number field is not generated by pseudo-regularizable elements. Let $F$ be a number field and let $X$ be a variety over $F$ of positive dimension, with function field $F(X)$. The Cremona group $\mathrm{Cr}_3(F(X))$, the group of birational automorphisms of affine $3$-space over $F(X)$, is not generated by its pseudo-regularizable elements.
nodes.title: $\mathrm{Cr}_3$ of a function field over a number field is not generated by pseudo-regularizable elements

nodes.summary: $\mathrm{Cr}_3$ of a function field over a finite field is not generated by pseudo-regularizable elements. Let $F$ be a finite field and let $X$ be a variety over $F$ of positive dimension, with function field $F(X)$. The Cremona group $\mathrm{Cr}_3(F(X))$, the group of birational automorphisms of affine $3$-space over $F(X)$, is not generated by its pseudo-regularizable elements.
nodes.title: $\mathrm{Cr}_3$ of a function field over a finite field is not generated by pseudo-regularizable elements

nodes.summary: $\mathrm{Cr}_3$ of a function field over an algebraically closed field is not generated by pseudo-regularizable elements. Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field and let $X$ be a variety over $F$ of positive dimension, with function field $F(X)$. The Cremona group $\mathrm{Cr}_3(F(X))$, the group of birational automorphisms of affine $3$-space over $F(X)$, is not generated by its pseudo-regularizable elements.
nodes.title: $\mathrm{Cr}_3$ of a function field over an algebraically closed field is not generated by pseudo-regularizable elements

nodes.summary: $\mathrm{Cr}_n$ of a subfield of $\mathbb{C}$ is not generated by pseudo-regularizable elements for $n \ge 4$. Let $k$ be a subfield of $\mathbb{C}$ and let $n \ge 4$. The Cremona group $\mathrm{Cr}_n(k)$, the group of birational automorphisms of affine $n$-space over $k$, is not generated by its pseudo-regularizable elements.
nodes.title: $\mathrm{Cr}_n$ of a subfield of $\mathbb{C}$ is not generated by pseudo-regularizable elements for $n \ge 4$

nodes.summary: $\mathrm{Cr}_n$ of an infinite field is not generated by pseudo-regularizable elements for $n \ge 5$. Let $k$ be an infinite field and let $n \ge 5$. The Cremona group $\mathrm{Cr}_n(k)$, the group of birational automorphisms of affine $n$-space over $k$, is not generated by its pseudo-regularizable elements.
nodes.title: $\mathrm{Cr}_n$ of an infinite field is not generated by pseudo-regularizable elements for $n \ge 5$

nodes.summary: Let $X$ and $Y$ be irreducible schemes and let $f$ be a partial isomorphism from $X$ to $Y$, that is, an isomorphism from a dense open subscheme of $X$ onto a dense open subscheme of $Y$. The birational map from $X$ to $Y$ given by $f$ has as forward map the rational map $X \dashrightarrow Y$ represented by $f$, and as inverse the rational map $Y \dashrightarrow X$ represented by the inverse of $f$.
nodes.title: Birational map of a partial isomorphism

nodes.summary: Let $X$, $Y$ and $Z$ be irreducible schemes, let $f$ be a birational map from $X$ to $Y$ and let $g$ be a birational map from $Y$ to $Z$. The composite of $f$ and $g$ is the birational map from $X$ to $Z$ whose forward rational map is the forward map of $f$ followed by the forward map of $g$, and whose inverse rational map is the inverse of $g$ followed by the inverse of $f$.
nodes.title: Composition of birational maps

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a field. A variety over $k$ in this sense is a scheme $X$ together with a morphism $X \to \operatorname{Spec} k$ such that $X$ is integral (irreducible and reduced) and the morphism is separated and of finite type (locally of finite type and quasi-compact).
nodes.title: Integral variety over a field

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
